title: Matuyama–Brunhes paleomagnetic reversal
summary: The Matuyama–Brunhes paleomagnetic reversal has an astronomical age of 772.9 ka at its directional midpoint in the Chiba section on Japan's Boso Peninsula. Because it is a primary guide globally, it marks the Early–Middle Pleistocene boundary, and the boundary stratotype is placed 1.1 m below that midpoint.

uncertainty.note: Astronomical age of the directional midpoint, 772.9 ± 5.4 ka (Head 2021); ICS gives the GSSP at 774.1 ± 5.0 ka. Years are ka counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

where.modern_name: Chiba section, Boso Peninsula, Chiba Prefecture, Japan (stratotype section; the reversal is a global signal)
where.historical_name: Boso Peninsula, Japan; no polities at this date

importance.justification: Its date anchors the base of the Middle Pleistocene and the Chibanian Stage and is a global dating marker.

sources.title: Review of the Early–Middle Pleistocene boundary and Marine Isotope Stage 19 (Progress in Earth and Planetary Science 8:50)
sources.publisher: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science (SpringerOpen), via PubMed Central
sources.author: Martin J. Head

reviewer_note: Least sure: the pin is the Chiba stratotype (ICS gives degrees-minutes-seconds, converted to decimal); the reversal itself is global. Head 2021 gives a slightly different coordinate range for the composite section. Ages are astronomical ages from two pages; other chronologies differ by about 1 kyr.
